post_content:
Most agency case studies are unfalsifiable. A percentage with no baseline, a graph with no axis labels, a client who cannot be contacted to confirm any of it. We would rather publish fewer of them and have each one checkable.

So this page has one entry on it. That is not because there is only one client — it is because a case study needs two things we will not fake: a client who has agreed to be named, and a result that was actually measured. Work that is too recent to have produced data does not get written up as though it had. When those engagements mature, they will appear here with their numbers, including the ones that did not go to plan.

Everything IT — consolidating a sprawling location-page structure

Client: Everything IT, a managed IT services provider based in Dublin, serving business clients across Ireland.
Work: Technical SEO, information architecture, content.
Period measured: 1–27 July 2026 against 1–27 August 2026, from Google Search Console.

The problem

The site had accumulated location pages the way most sites accumulate them: gradually, by different people, with no plan. Multiple URLs targeted the same city — /cork/, /it-support-cork/ and /it-support-cork-2/ all existed simultaneously. The copy across them was close to identical with the city name swapped, which is the doorway pattern Google filters rather than rewards. The pages competed with each other for the same searches, and none of them won.

What we did

  • Cut the location pages down to four. Cork, Galway, Limerick and Waterford — the four regions where Everything IT genuinely has something specific to offer. Everything else was retired and redirected rather than left to dilute the site.
  • Wrote each of the four differently. Not a template with the city swapped. Cork City and County Cork, Galway and the West, Limerick and the Mid-West, Waterford and the South-East each serve a different mix of local businesses, so each page targets the services that actually match its area.
  • Resolved the duplicate URLs. One canonical page per location, with 301s from the retired variants so the accumulated equity moved rather than evaporated.
  • Rebuilt internal linking between the location pages and the location directory, so the four surviving pages inherited the internal authority the retired ones had been splitting.

The result

Across the four surviving pages, comparing the month before the work with the month after:

PageClicksImpressionsAverage position
Cork4 → 71,159 → 87645.7 → 34.4
Waterford3 → 31,207 → 69851.6 → 36.2
Limerick7 → 9928 → 2,10117.5 → 27.8
Galway5 → 6899 → 1,27143.5 → 40.4
Combined19 → 254,193 → 4,946—

Clicks to the four pages rose 32% and impressions 18%. On individual commercial searches, the page-one movement is the part that matters more than the totals: business IT support Waterford averaged position 2.5, IT services Limerick around 5, IT support Limerick around 7, and network specialists Cork 9.5.

What did not go to plan

Two things, stated plainly because a case study that reports only the good half is an advertisement.

Limerick's average position got worse — 17.5 to 27.8 — while its impressions more than doubled. Those two facts are related. The page went from surfacing for a narrow set of searches to surfacing for a much wider set, and the newly-added ones sit lower down. An average dragged down by winning more ground is not the same as a decline, but it looks identical on a dashboard, and any agency reporting on this account should be able to tell you which one you are looking at.

Cork and Waterford both lost impressions even as their positions improved sharply. During a consolidation the retired URLs keep appearing in search results for a while, then stop; the totals dip before they recover. We expected this and said so in advance, which is the only reason it was not alarming when it happened.

Across the whole domain, including every retired URL bleeding its old traffic through a redirect, the same month looked flat. Judged only on the four pages that were actually the subject of the work, it did not. Both numbers are true, and an agency that shows you only the flattering one is choosing which truth to hand you.

Still in progress

An AI chat assistant for the site has been built and is running on a staging environment for the client to evaluate before any decision about putting it in front of real visitors. It is mentioned here because it is part of the engagement, not because there is a result to report yet. There is not.

Why the list is short

Other work is underway — website builds and search work for clients in Arizona and elsewhere. It is not on this page for one of two reasons: the site has not launched yet, so there is nothing to measure, or the client has not been asked whether they want to be named and we are not going to assume.

That is a slower way to build a portfolio page. It is also the reason the one entry above can be checked line by line.

FAQ

Why are there so few case studies here?

Because we only publish work where the client agreed to be named and where there is something measured to report. Engagements that are too new to have produced data are not written up as though they had.

Do you work with clients outside Arizona?

Yes. Everything IT is in Ireland and the work was delivered from Gilbert, Arizona. Technical SEO, content and reporting do not require the agency to be in the same country. Where physical presence genuinely matters, such as photography or in-person meetings, we say so before the engagement starts.

Will you show my results publicly?

Only if you tell us we can. Nothing is published about your account without your explicit agreement, and you can withdraw that at any point and we will take it down.

Do you guarantee results like these?

No. One engagement is not a forecast for another. Different market, different competition, different starting point. Anyone guaranteeing a specific position is either inexperienced or not being straight with you.

Ask us about work we have not published

If you want to see something closer to your own situation, ask. There is work we cannot put on a public page but can walk you through on a call, and we can usually put you in touch with the client directly.
